transcription.tex: \text{[MAT 2008 1C] For which angles in 0 ≤ θ < 2π are these simultaneous equations solvable?}
\text{A: all angles; B: all except one; C: all except two; D: all except three.}

\text{Let \(s=\sin\theta\) and \(c=\cos\theta\). Multiply the first equation by s and the second by c, then subtract:\[(s^2+c^2)y=c-2s\]\[y=c-2s\]Similarly, eliminate y:\[x=2c+s\]Both are defined for every θ. Answer A.}
\text{No division by a potentially zero sine or cosine is required. Dividing by one could incorrectly exclude valid angles.}
